name: Ui_ArcListRow_BlendPoseToTarget
summary: Per-row animation step of the arc list: eases the row's snapshot start/end points (f_4AC/f_4B8) toward the target vectors (f_4D4/f_4E0) that Ui_ArcListWindow_LayoutEntriesByHeight writes, using the period at battleWork+0x569C, then renormalises the forward vector f_1C..f_24 and applies the lateral offsets. Returns 1 so it can act as a row update slot.
evidence: Six vtables hold it (0x772D30, 0x7750A4, 0x775178, 0x777D8C, 0x779B44, 0x77CEF0), each placing it immediately after the confident Ui_ArcListWindow_LayoutEntriesByHeight, which itself writes the f_4D4/f_4E0 targets this function interpolates toward; the row pose helper Ui_ArcListRow_UpdateSwingPose (0x49DDB8) has the same f_4..f_18 output layout. The readable body is damaged decompilation (coprocessor_ helpers, bad-instruction warnings), so the verdict rests on the disassembly and the vtable neighbourhood rather than on the Ghidra control flow.

name: maybe_Battle_Ui_MemberScreen_UpdateMemberPoses
summary: Member-model layout sub-update of the battle member panel: resolves the leader and marker models, builds each member's follow transform (leader offset or target marker), steers the facing with acos/sin, writes the model positions and creates the target-marker sprite. Returns 1.
evidence: Its only caller is Battle_Ui_MemberScreen_UpdateB (0x005990F8; the `bl 0x5988A8` is at 0x599484), which passes its battle member-screen pointer, and the body also calls maybe_Ui_BattleTargetMarker_CreateFromModelId and reads the battle work at work+0x5C. The old FieldParty prefix came from the party-looking accessors, but this is the battle member screen's placement step.

name: maybe_Gfx_EffectPart_BindRelativeTransform
summary: Builds the transform of an effect part relative to another actor (rotation delta from the two 2x2 bases at f_8C..f_98 via acos/cos/sin) and binds it with Gfx_EffectPart_BindByName using the part's relative name string at self+4. The old name claimed a pose copy; the disassembly shows the final call is the effect-part binder with a 12-float parameter block.
evidence: Disassembly 0x162D54-0x162D70 loads r0 = partner (result of 0x005B1208), r1 = self, r2 = self->f_4 relative name and r3 = the 12-float block built on the stack, then `bl #0x5f56a0` = Gfx_EffectPart_BindByName. That is a bind with parameters, not a copy; the readable C dropped three quarters of the call.

name: maybe_Gfx_UpdateActorsInViewCone
signature: void maybe_Gfx_UpdateActorsInViewCone(void* unused, const float* position, const float* direction)
summary: Walks the field actor list (work+0x54, list id 4) and, for actors of class 0x7C3684 that pass the state checks, measures the vertical/horizontal distance and the angle between the given direction and the offset; actors inside the radius and cone receive a vtable+0x38(0x1B, 0) update call. It does not build a billboard basis.
evidence: The body never writes a basis: it is the same list walk and cone test that appears in maybe_Camera_UpdateFollowPosition_2 (same 0x7A6408 angle scale, same +0x38 slot with 0x1B), and its only caller Ui_SpriteMarker_SetTargetFromActor passes a position plus a direction. The old name described what the caller wanted, not what this body does.

name: Actor_CheckInteractionRange
summary: Talk-range gate of the field actor: checks the actor's interaction target is inside the summed capsule radii and the actor's facing cone, plays the idle/talk animation and accumulates the interaction timer f_38; returns 1 once the timer lies inside the actor's f_348 window.
evidence: New named caller Actor_UpdateApproachMove (0x227934) uses the return value to trigger maybe_Camera_UpdateFollowPosition and func_005E7848(actor,3,0) (the arrive/talk notification), so the routine really is the talk-range/arrival gate. The named callee maybe_Field_Actor_PlayIdleAnimation and the 'Walk'/'Run' literals confirm the animation side.

name: Field_Action_HorseTurn
signature: void Field_Action_HorseTurn(float* out, const HorseAction* self, const float* inputDir, float speed)
summary: Turn step of the horse/run action: below the speed threshold it rotates the current reference heading (camera forward, or self f_2C..f_34) toward inputDir by at most f_40 degrees and writes the result; above it, it lerps the heading toward inputDir and renormalises.
evidence: It belongs to the class whose vtable 0x762B78 also holds maybe_Field_Action_InitHorseParams, maybe_Field_Action_MoveStep and Field_Action_Horse_CheckCanContinue, and is entered from that class's 0x303480 vtable slot (`bl 0x3038CC` at 0x303714). The signature gains the turn-scale float that the ABI passes in s0 and Ghidra dropped.

name: maybe_Monster_BehaviorAction_Start
summary: Virtual slot 1 (start) of a monster field-behaviour action: copies the actor's orientation/scale block (f_5F4..), derives the turn/aim angles and playback rates, then starts the nested state machine (state vtable f_14(flag), then f_10()).
evidence: Its vtable 0x7688B4 is slot 1 of the class whose constructor 0x003AF5A4 installs vtable 0x007688AC, i.e. the same maybe_Monster_BehaviorAction_* family as the named siblings SyncEffectAndAnim (0x003AF504) and UpdateBlend (0x003AF454). So the FieldBehaviour prefix and the specific 'BeginAttack' claim were both wrong; the body is the generic action start.

name: maybe_Camera_ShouldRefreshPathPoint
signature: u32 maybe_Camera_ShouldRefreshPathPoint(void* cam, const float* reference, const float* point, const float* dir, float angleLimit)
summary: Geometric predicate used by the camera path updater: given a reference point, a candidate point, a forward direction and an angle limit (in s0) it returns 0 when the candidate is within the table's max distance (row f_1C) and inside the cone, and 1 when the point is out of range, out of the cone, or effectively on the reference point.
evidence: All three call sites are Camera_UpdateWorkPath (0x1D3330, 0x1D359C) and maybe_Camera_UpdateWorkPathEx (0x1D40A8), and every one of them refreshes the path point only when the result is non-zero; so this is an 'is the point out of range/cone' test, not an NPC movement step. The Game_GetDataManager row read func_0063D928 supplies the max distance.

name: maybe_Field_CheckGimmickItemGetFlag
summary: Tail block of the IsGimmickItemGetTimming native (0x0015EBFC): resolves the game-object handle and returns the signed status byte at object+0x2B4, or 1 when the handle does not resolve. The readable C at this address is a misdecompilation of unrelated float code.
evidence: The disassembly evidence in the header is still the only reliable source and is unchanged: asm/text/text_00140048.s shows this block is entered from 0x0015EBFC, calls 0x0044C3D0 (handle->object lookup) and 0x0064E130 (ldrsh [obj+0x2B4]). The Ghidra file here is damaged, which is exactly why the name stays below 0.5 rather than being promoted.

name: maybe_Field_Action_EvaluateTurnDirection
signature: void maybe_Field_Action_EvaluateTurnDirection(float* unused, const HorseAction* self, float* out, void* ctx)
summary: Computes the desired heading for the horse/run action: rotates the actor's current 2x2 basis by the input yaw (s0, self->f_44), orthonormalises it, then hands it to Field_Action_HorseTurn for the turn-rate clamp/lerp and copies the result to out.
evidence: It is a slot of both the run action (vtable 0x762B2C) and the horse action (0x762BA4, next to Field_Action_Horse_CheckCanContinue), and asm/text shows the direct `bl 0x3038CC` at 0x303714 with (sp, self, out, ctx). That makes it the Field_Action turn-direction evaluator rather than an Anim aim pose.

name: Anim_BlendTransform
signature: void Anim_BlendTransform(float* out, const AnimTransform* a, const AnimTransform* b, float t)
summary: Blends two 3D poses by the factor t: lerps the position triple and slerps the quaternion at +0xC..+0x18, writing seven floats (position + quaternion) to out. Used by the motion/anim-object blend update.
evidence: Both callers are now named: maybe_Motion_UpdateBlendTimer (0x4D4414) and maybe_AnimObject_UpdateAttachmentPoint (0x4D4898), which store the seven-float result in their blend slots. There is no other Motion_ function in the binary while Anim_ is the established prefix, and the body's lerp + quaternion slerp is exactly a pose blend.

name: maybe_Math_RebuildBasis
summary: Repairs a stored rotation block: takes the first two axes, builds the third by cross product, rotates it by the angle pair at +0x18/+0x1C and renormalises, writing a valid first axis back into basis[0..2]. Called immediately before the block is converted to a matrix.
evidence: All three callers (Gfx_EffectPart_UpdateTransform 0x5F7A10, maybe_Trail_UpdateGeometry 0x5F6668, maybe_Field_ActorAction_UpdateModelRotation 0x372D38) call it right before func_00573144 (basis->matrix), and the body reads basis[0..5] as two existing axes plus basis[6]/basis[7] as the angle pair. It does not build a basis from an angle triple, so the old name was wrong.

name: maybe_Battle_IsUnitInEffectRange
signature: u32 maybe_Battle_IsUnitInEffectRange(void* self, float* outDistance, BattleUnit* source, BattleUnit* target, EffectRange* range)
summary: Range/angle predicate between two battle units: normalises the horizontal offset, rejects when the distance does not match the wanted relation or the facing angle exceeds range->f_10 (unless range->f_18 says to ignore the angle), and returns the distance through outDistance. Returns 1 when the target is in range.
evidence: Its only caller is maybe_Battle_Action_SelectEffectTarget (0x635948, two call sites) and arguments 3/4 are two battle units with orientation bases at +8..+14; the return value gates target selection. Nothing here computes an effect transform, so the old name was misleading.

name: maybe_Ui_JackpotScreen_UpdateReelResult
summary: Per-state update of the jackpot reel screen: compares the two reel models' state bytes, and when both have stopped it detects a winning line from the direction dot (threshold 0.95), sets the model state and plays the win SEs; while the payout runs it advances the payout thresholds, sets f_144 when a payout mark is reached and caches the last payout position in f_1CC.
evidence: Its vtable 0x72AA54 places it between Ui_JackpotScreen_StartPayout and maybe_Ui_JackpotScreen_HandleInput in the jackpot screen state table, and the body handles both the two-reel comparison and the whole payout animation, so 'CompareReels' described only the first branch.

name: Ui_JockeyPanel_Teardown
summary: Teardown of the jockey panel: plays the panel close sound through the UI core player, stops the cached sound handle f_14C and the preview channel f_148 and clears both.
evidence: Its vtable 0x728508 sits next to Ui_JockeyPanel_Close / maybe_Ui_JockeyPanel_UpdateCursor / maybe_Ui_JockeyPanel_ResetMode, and the named callees Ui_GetCore, Sound_GetPlayer and maybe_Sound_StopBgmHandle confirm the panel teardown. It has no direct caller because it is a vtable slot, which is expected here.

name: maybe_Sound_LookupGainFromTable
signature: void maybe_Sound_LookupGainFromTable(u32 id, u32 count, u32 payload)
summary: Looks a value up in an array addressed by a caller-supplied base plus (id>>1) and an index, bounds-checks it against count>>2 and applies it as a voice gain via Sound_SetVoiceGainByHandle. The arguments snapshotted into the Sound_GetPlayer frame are still unclear.
evidence: The readable body is damaged Thumb code (unaff_r4/r5/r6, in_CY) and the asm/text block at 0x163650 is misaligned, so the only usable signal is the callee set - Sound_GetPlayer, VectorUnsignedToFloat and Sound_SetVoiceGainByHandle - which indicates a gain lookup, not the BGM playback the old name claimed. Kept low until the Thumb disassembly is repaired.

name: maybe_Field_Action_StepBegin
summary: Start hook of the field step action: calls Field_Actor_BeginStep (turn the movement visuals on and record the facing), invalidates the current step SE id (f_80 = 0xFFFF) and releases the previous voice handle f_74 so Field_Action_PlayStepSound starts a fresh footstep.
evidence: Vtable 0x762924 lists it as the slot right before maybe_Field_Action_StepEnd and the confident Field_Action_PlayStepSound, and its body calls maybe_Field_Actor_BeginStep, the begin half of the step action. 'StopMove' described the wrong operation: nothing stops a move here.

name: maybe_Field_Action_StepEnd
summary: End hook of the field step action: calls Field_Actor_EndBehaviour (turn the movement visuals off) and releases the footstep voice handle f_74. Mirror of 0x003017E0.
evidence: Same vtable (0x762924) as maybe_Field_Action_StepBegin and Field_Action_PlayStepSound, and the body calls maybe_Field_Actor_EndBehaviour, whose only caller is this routine. 'StopStepSound' captured only half of what the slot does.

name: Party_BuildMemberIdList
signature: void Party_BuildMemberIdList(u8* out, u32 count, u32 arg4)
summary: Builds the list of party member ids usable in the field: walks the party count at work+0x27218, resolves each entry through the bag at work+0x24A98 and the member record func_0035EB98, keeps members that are not flagged dead (bit 0x20 at +0xDA), are present in the overlay table (+0x254 == 1) and have a non-zero id, and appends them to the output buffer.
evidence: The established facts identify func_0035EB98 as the party member record and work+0x24A98 as the bag, and the body also reads the party count at work+0x27218 - exactly a party-id list build. The readable decompilation is damaged (unaff_r6/r7/r8; the vector insert loop is modelled as non-returning memmove calls), so confidence sits at the lower end of the confirm range.

name: maybe_Ui_DialogUpdateQueue
signature: u32 maybe_Ui_DialogUpdateQueue(void* self, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Page-queue step of the dialog object: when the page list [f_4A4,f_4A8) is empty it sets the pending-page flag at work+0x27220 and runs the embedded handler's vtable +0x14/+0x10 pair; otherwise it pops the next page id and calls the page advance helper func_001675B8.
evidence: The new context only confirms the family: the embedded handler at self+0x11C is a vtable object and work+0x27220 is the pending-page flag the message code also uses. There is still no named caller, and the queue owner could be the message window rather than the dialog object, so the name stays maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_FilterIdListByRecord
signature: void maybe_Ui_FilterIdListByRecord(void* self, const u8* filter)
summary: Filters a byte list of model/object ids in place: for each source byte it resolves the record via func_0063D338 and appends the id to [f_6C,f_70) when the record is kind 2 and matches the five-byte filter record (id pair + attribute byte). The source list lives in self+4..self+8.
evidence: Its only caller is maybe_Model_BuildUiFilterRecord (0x1CB2F8), which fills exactly that five-byte record from model fields, so the routine filters ids by record rather than by a plain id as the old name said. There is no other caller, so the subsystem prefix stays Ui_.

name: maybe_Container_RemoveFromGlobalList
summary: Removes an object from the global registry vector g_uniqueIdPoolTable, shifts the tail down, unlinks its +0x60 node through func_005647F8 and clears the object's f_E4 flag.
evidence: The new context places it in the object-registry vtable 0x758B44 (beside Sound_Emitter_Dtor, Sound_Listener_Dtor and Gfx_Sprite_CreateInstance), which fits global list membership, but the registry's owner is still unknown and there is no direct caller, so the name stays maybe_.

name: maybe_Container_PopByteLookup
summary: Pops one byte from a byte vector (end pointer decremented) and returns the 8-byte record with that index from the pool table reached through 0x007A909C, or null when the index is out of range.
evidence: The vtable hit at 0x75B3B0 puts it beside UI/message-window slots rather than a pure container class, which weakens the Container prefix, but the pop+index body itself is unchanged and still matches the old description. Kept at maybe_.

name: maybe_Ui_TextStyle_AppendDescriptor
summary: Lazily builds the shared text-style descriptor table (flag 0x7BE30C, table 0x7BE310, 0xA24 bytes, constructor vtable 0x782990), resolves the 8-byte style record for a tag and appends its pointer to the caller's pointer vector when the record has a payload.
evidence: The globals and allocation are identical to the named maybe_Ui_TextStyle_GetDescriptor (0x1A5B60): same 0x7BE30C one-time flag, same 0x7BE310 table, size 0xA24 and constructor 0x0011CFDC/0x00782990. This routine resolves the per-tag record with 0x0063D2C4 from that same table object and appends the record instead of returning it, so it belongs to the text-style family but never formats text.

name: Container_SmallVectorCopyConstruct
summary: Copy-constructs a five-element small vector: installs the inline buffer at self+0x10 (begin = end = self+0x10, cap = self+0x24), then copies the source range and takes the standard length-error path when the source holds more than five elements.
evidence: The self-referential begin/end/cap layout and the five-element capacity check are the inlined small-vector copy constructor, and both call sites (maybe_Container_SmallVectorInitFrom 0x617BDC and maybe_Ui_MessagePanel_ExecStateA 0x3B0B18) copy a range of 4-byte elements. Ghidra renders the copy loop as non-returning memmove calls, but the structure is unambiguous.

name: maybe_Container_IndexedArray_GetElement
summary: Iterator-style accessor: reads the current byte index from the container cursor and returns a pointer to the 8-byte record with that index in the table reached through self+4 (+0x354), or null when out of range; the bounds failure goes to the standard assert path.
evidence: The new vtable context (0x75DD84, beside Ui_CompositeWindow_DtorB and Ui_StatusWindow_UpdateState) does not identify the 8-byte records, and the bounds path also decrements the container's f_C, so 'GetElement' remains an inference rather than a proven accessor shape. Kept at maybe_.

name: std_String_AppendCharB
signature: void std_String_AppendCharB(std_String* str, const char* end)
summary: Out-of-line growth path of std::string::push_back: appends one character to the string (begin at +0, end at +4, capacity at +8), reallocating and copying the old range when the end pointer has reached the capacity.
evidence: The three-pointer begin/end/capacity layout is std::string, and the inlined caller maybe_Ui_Panel_BuildAttributeText appends a byte only when its local cursor equals the end pointer, i.e. precisely on capacity exhaustion. That is push_back, not the generic range append the old name claimed; the B suffix distinguishes it from the SSO fast path std_String_AppendChar at 0x21BC88.

name: maybe_std_String_AppendRange
signature: void maybe_std_String_AppendRange(std_String* str, const char* end)
summary: Second out-of-line instantiation of the std::string append/growth path: same begin/end/capacity triple, but with a longer inlined copy of a byte range, used by the event id-set text builder.
evidence: Same prologue and three-pointer string layout as std_String_AppendChar, but the body is 692 bytes and its only caller (maybe_Event_UpdateIdSet, 0x1E7724) appends multi-byte text. The copy loop is still lost behind non-returning memmove calls, so the name stays just below 0.5.

name: maybe_Battle_CommandSlots_UpdateContinuationA
summary: Not an entry point: a mid-routine fragment of the ARM function at 0x00168C64 (Ghidra split it at a jump target). It iterates the five 0x8C-byte command slots, dispatches each slot object's vtable+0x10 and writes or inserts the resulting battle action slots through Battle_WriteActionSlot / Battle_InsertActionSlot.
evidence: There is no push at 0x00169076 and r4/r6 are live on entry; the code at 0x169074 is mid-block and the routine only returns at 0x001690EC, so this is a split fragment, not a function. The named callees (Battle_InsertActionSlot, Battle_WriteActionSlot, func_0063FD24 action rows, battle work work+0x5C and its +0x4260 party list) identify it as battle command-slot handling; the old Ui_Widget name came from the false Thumb prologue.

name: maybe_Battle_CommandSlots_UpdateContinuationB
summary: Second split fragment of the same ARM routine (0x00168C64): the loop body that dispatches each queued command slot's vtable method, creates the per-slot command object from the 0x7A4338/0x7A4268 tables and queues the action entry.
evidence: Starts four bytes after 0x00169076 with identical code and no prologue, and still lies inside the routine that returns at 0x001690EC; the same named battle-queue callees apply. A continuation fragment cannot have a meaningful standalone name, so this is labelled as such instead of keeping the invented Ui_Widget name.

name: Battle_QueueCommandByCategory
summary: Queues the default command entry for a battle unit: lets the action object fill its six-byte descriptor, maps the unit's category byte (+0x31) to action id 0xE/2/3 in the auto-battle mode (work+0x4244) and otherwise uses id 1, then pushes or inserts the entry via Battle_CommandQueue_PushEntry / Battle_InsertActionSlot according to the unit's +0xB0F7 flag.
evidence: Both queue functions and the action-id ladder are now readable, so the routine does not merely resolve a type - it enqueues the entry. It is itself a handler in the action dispatch table at 0x726AB0 (between maybe_Battle_QueueAbilityActionVariant and Battle_QueueAbilityAction), i.e. the 'queue this unit's default command' slot.

name: Battle_DispatchUnitAction
signature: void Battle_DispatchUnitAction(BattleManager* self, BattleUnit* unit, u32 actionId, int** outEntry)
summary: Dispatches one unit's pending action: reads its category and sub-ids from +0xB0F7/+0xB0F9 (or the alternate block), invokes the matching handler from the manager's eleven-slot function table, and falls back to enqueuing generic action 0x14; finishes by calling the unit's vtable+0x48(1).
evidence: Caller Battle_ProcessUnitActions (0x16ECE4 and 0x16ED20) plus the tail call from Battle_SelectActionTargets show it running as the action dispatch step, and the function-table lookup (self + category*8, category < 0xB) with the 0x14 fallback is exactly the dispatch-or-default pattern the name claims.

name: Battle_QueueAttackActions
summary: Enqueues the two-step attack sequence for a unit: action 0xD (attack) followed by 0x2E (finish), appended through Battle_CommandQueue_PushEntry or inserted through Battle_InsertActionSlot depending on the unit's +0xB0F7 mode, with the follow-up flag derived from the alive/state bytes.
evidence: In the action-handler table at 0x726AB0 it sits between Battle_QueueAbilityAction and Battle_ExecuteItemAction, i.e. it is the normal-attack handler, and both queue calls are now named with the exact action ids 0xD and 0x2E.

name: Battle_ResetCommandQueue
summary: Empties the battle command list (Battle_FreeCommandList walks the intrusive list at +0x110) and clears the queue-dirty byte at +0x13D.
evidence: The named callee Battle_FreeCommandList makes the reset explicit, and the vtable at 0x75832C (beside Battle_Update / Battle_Initialize) is the battle manager's; both callers are teardown paths (BattleScene_ReleaseSceneModels, Ui_CompositeWindow_ReleaseHandles).

name: Battle_Destroy
summary: Destructor of the battle manager: reinstalls the base vtable, destroys the optional child dispatcher at self[0x39], frees the command list through Battle_FreeCommandList and unlinks the manager from its owner's doubly linked list.
evidence: The body begins with `*self = &g_battleManagerVtable` and then calls Battle_FreeCommandList, and its vtable hit at 0x758308 lies in the battle manager vtable block. It is the out-of-line destructor, so 'Destroy' is accurate; the two tail callers are cleanup paths.

name: Battle_CollectGroupTargets
signature: uint32_t Battle_CollectGroupTargets(BattleManager* self, BattleAction* action, BattleUnit* source, int groupIndex)
summary: Collects the units of one group (work+0x428C + groupIndex*0x1C) that match the source's target mode (unit vtable+0x10/+0x18) into action+0x20 and returns their count; when the group's first unit is valid it becomes the action's primary target, and with no primary target the walk repeats over all four groups.
evidence: Caller Battle_SelectActionTargets (0x170E28) and callee Battle_IsTargetValid show the routine filling the action's target array, and the return value is the number of targets, so 'Collect...Targets' describes the work better than 'Select', which is the caller's job.

name: maybe_Battle_SelectTargetsMode8
signature: void maybe_Battle_SelectTargetsMode8(Battle* battle, u32 arg2, u32 arg3, u32 arg4)
summary: Target-selection handler for mode 8: calls Battle_SelectActionTargets(battle, arg4, arg3, 8) and then constructs the four 8-byte target descriptors with the 0x005906C0 constructor. The recovered body is truncated after the array constructor.
evidence: It is the next entry in the mode table at 0x726B18 after Battle_SelectTargetsMode4/5/6, which fixes both the naming pattern and the mode argument 8; the old 'Queue' was wrong because the function only selects and formats targets.

name: Battle_SelectTargetsThunk
summary: Register-preserving thunk to Battle_SelectActionTargets, used where the caller has already placed the arguments in r0-r4.
evidence: The disassembly is `bl 0x170D4C; bx lr` with untouched registers, and its only caller maybe_Battle_RunTargetSelection (0x20A19C) reaches it directly. A thunk with no locals is exactly what the name says.

name: Ui_BattleWindow_CloseCommandList
summary: Closes the command list of the battle party window: asks the window script to advance to step 0x12, stores the current page on the command pane, refreshes the party rows and hides the target window.
evidence: Its vtable 0x728CFC lies between Ui_PartyPanel_SwapMembers and maybe_Ui_BattleWindow_HideTargetWindow, and the named callees maybe_Ui_PartyPanel_RefreshMemberIds, Ui_PartyPanel_RefreshRows and Ui_BattleTargetWindow_Hide make the close path explicit.

name: maybe_Battle_CloseBattleScene
summary: Short sibling of maybe_Battle_FinishBattleScene: calls the current battle actor's presentation object vtable+0x28 and hides the target window; it spawns no popup and writes no state.
evidence: This is a real 80-byte function (push {r3,lr} at 0x1715C4, pop {r3,pc} at 0x171610), but which of the two close/finish variants the callers pick is still unclear: 0x1714D4 pairs +0x18/+0x74 with a popup, this one only calls +0x28. Kept at maybe_ until the +0x28 slot is identified.
